stories.headline: Flood fury in AP as rivers swell
stories.title: Flood fury in AP as rivers swell
stories.summary: Flood warnings issued as Vamsadhara, Nagavali swell
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amaravati: Following heavy rains over the past four days triggered by the severe depression that crossed the state coast, Andhra Pradesh remained on high flood alert on Friday as the continual downpour sent large volumes of water into rivers, reservoirs, and barrages.
The latest reservoir data showed substantial inflows into several projects, with authorities releasing much of the incoming water downstream to maintain storage levels and regulate flood flows.
The impact was particularly pronounced in Srikakulam, where the Vamsadhara and Nagavali rivers continued to swell following heavy rainfall in the district and upstream areas of Odisha.
A first danger warning remained in force at Gotta Barrage, where the latest reservoir data showed an inflow of 44,900 cusecs and outflow of 45,679 cusecs.
At Narayanapuram Anicut, inflow and outflow were both around 66,900 cusecs, with officials maintaining a close watch on the rising flood levels.
Residents in low-lying and riverbank areas have been advised to remain alert.
The Nagavali was also receiving heavy flows from the upstream catchment, besides water released from Thotapalli and Madduvalasa projects.
Thotapalli recorded 23,250 cusecs each of inflow and outflow, while Madduvalasa received 25,100 cusecs and released 26,000 cusecs.
Flood waters have begun entering agricultural fields in villages in Burja and Amadalavalasa mandals.
The Prakasam Barrage in Vijayawada was also receiving a major surge, with 40,521 cusecs of inflow and an equal quantity being released downstream.
Flood waters from the Munneru, Kattaleru and Budameru streams contributed to the sharp rise, prompting the opening of 20 gates.
This was the first major surplus release from the barrage this season.

stories.headline: 'Glaciers, floods don't travel with visas': Nepal PM's India-China appeal
stories.title: 'Glaciers, floods don't travel with visas': Nepal PM's India-China appeal
stories.summary: In his maiden address to UN General Assembly, Shah, 36, said, “Glaciers and floods do not travel with a visa stamped on passports.” His address on Thursday came during his first foreign trip since taking office on March 27.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: Nepal PM Balendra Shah called on India and China to join a trilateral Himalayan climate resilience mechanism to share satellite data, jointly monitor dangerous glacial lakes, strengthen early-warning systems and coordinate cross-border disaster response, telling UN General Assembly that climate change “does not recognise borders” after the Aug 26 deluge left at least 1,400 dead and more than 6,000 missing.

In his maiden address to UN General Assembly, Shah, 36, said, “Glaciers and floods do not travel with a visa stamped on passports.” His address on Thursday came during his first foreign trip since taking office on March 27.
He thanked India and China for their “prompt and generous assistance” after the disaster.

Shah said warming was destabilising fragile Himalayan ecology by thawing permafrost, weakening mountain slopes and increasing risks from ice-rock avalanches, floods, landslides and other cascading hazards.
The Aug 26 disaster, he said, devastated both sides of Nepal-China border before floodwaters continued downstream towards India.
Nepal’s rapid assessment put physical recovery needs at around 10% of GDP.

Proposing a “Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism, led by Nepal, India and China”, Shah said the Hindu Kush Himalaya supported nearly two billion people through water, ecosystems, agriculture and livelihoods.
“Let the Himalayas be a laboratory for international cooperation, not a border of fragmented information,” he said.
Shah said Nepal contributed less than 0.1% of global greenhouse-gas emissions but was bearing a disproportionate cost.
“We did not create this crisis.
Yet we are paying a colossal price for it,” he said, arguing that countries contributing least to global warming should not be pushed further into debt to rebuild after climate disasters.

“When a climate-driven disaster destroys the infrastructure of a poor country, the answer cannot simply be another mega loan or a patchwork of small grants,” Shah said, seeking adequate grant-based financing and calling resources available through existing international climate funds inadequate.

stories.headline: Mamata Banerjee, CPI(M) bridge decades-old divide over Election Commission concerns
stories.title: Mamata Banerjee, CPI(M) bridge decades-old divide over Election Commission concerns
stories.summary: The chief of the Mamata Trinamool Congress is one of the first leaders to respond to CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby’s appeal for a broader Opposition consultation on issues surrounding the EC
reasons: source: event has 4 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 3 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: Setting aside decades-long differences, former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee spoke to CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby on Friday, with both leaders converging on the question of the “declining credibility” of the Election Commission (EC).
The call is unprecedented and comes against the backdrop of a rivalry spanning nearly three decades.
Ms. Banerjee quit the Congress to form the Trinamool Congress in 1997 because she believed the Congress’s State leadership was too soft on the ruling CPI(M)-led Left Front.
In 2011, she managed to defeat the 34-year-old Left Front government.
The CPI(M) remained the most strident critic of Ms. Banerjee’s 15-year reign, which ended with the 2026 Assembly elections.

Friday's phone call came as a result of an outreach led by Mr. Baby, who, following the recent Indian Express report that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar allegedly ignored objections raised by fellow Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi regarding various decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, wrote to leaders of multiple political parties exhorting them to respond to the "extraordinary situation".
Mr. Baby wrote the letter, dated September 23, 2026, to parties working both within and outside the Opposition INDIA bloc.
Beyond the INDIA bloc, he reached out to the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), and the Biju Janata Dal (BJD).
He also sent the same appeal to the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which is not registered as a political party.

In his letter, Mr. Baby wrote that to protect "constitutional values" and "citizens' right to vote", it is essential that all political outfits meet and deliberate with the "urgency that the situation warrants".

“The people of our country are looking at us with the hope that all of us will stand in defence of democracy, secularism and the right to vote," he said, asking the parties to find a mutually convenient date and place for the meeting.
Ms. Banerjee, according to sources, was one of the first leaders to respond to Mr. Baby’s plea.

stories.headline: Election Commission must respond to SIR irregularity allegations, says Ram Madhav
stories.title: Election Commission must respond to SIR irregularity allegations, says Ram Madhav
stories.summary: BJP leader says Opposition should not contest elections if it believes the electoral system is rigged
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national vice-president V. Ram Madhav said on Friday that the Election Commission of India (ECI) would have to respond to allegations of large-scale irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
He also indicated that Narendra Modi would remain the BJP’s prime ministerial candidate, saying that Mr. Modi would win two or three more elections.

Addressing a memorial lecture, ‘Ism Nee Payanam Etu’, after releasing the book Jaateeya Bhavam Karuvaina Communistlu here, Mr. Ram Madhav said the Congress and other Opposition parties should decide whether their victories in Kerala, Karnataka and Telangana were achieved because of “crumbs” from the BJP.
He said the Opposition should not contest elections if it genuinely believed that the electoral system was rigged.
In an apparent reference to Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Abhijit Dipke and others, Mr. Ram Madhav said some young leaders were emerging but lacked political maturity.

He said they were advising Opposition parties to stay away from what they described as “fixed matches” and “rigged elections”, while claiming that the Opposition had secured small, isolated victories with the BJP’s support.
“Is it so?” he asked the Opposition parties.
Mr. Ram Madhav also criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and questioned how he had concluded that the ECI was helping the BJP win elections.
If that were the case, he said, the ECI constituted by the Congress before 2014 was in place when elections were held in 2014, 2015 and 2016.

Responding to criticism of Mr. Modi’s electoral victories, he said that if the Prime Minister had won three elections without popular support, it was pertinent to recall that Jawaharlal Nehru had also won three elections.
Mr. Modi would win more elections because of his commitment and dedication to uplifting the last person in society, or Antyodaya, he said.

Mr. Ram Madhav said the concept of Antyodaya, articulated by Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya to ensure that the benefits of development reached the last person in society, was reflected in the welfare programmes of the Narendra Modi government.

stories.headline: Chirag and Upendra Kushwaha ask Election Commission to dispel confusion in minds of the people
stories.title: Chirag and Upendra Kushwaha ask Election Commission to dispel confusion in minds of the people
stories.summary: Union Minister and LJP(RV) leader says if questions are being raised about the Commission, then it is the responsibility of the Commission, and specifically Gyanesh Kumar, to strongly present his own side
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Bharatiya Janata Party felt the heat within its alliance over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise on Friday, as Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) leader Chirag Paswan and Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLM) leader Upendra Kushwaha urged the Election Commission of India (EC) to dispel confusion in the minds of the people.

Both Bihar leaders issued statements amid the demand of the Congress that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign immediately after an Indian Express report claimed that two of the three Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had formally recorded objections at least 14 times over the last 10 months.
He further said, “The Commission should present its position strongly to the people, and that is the beauty of democracy.
If people lose confidence in the election process or if doubts arise, then it’s wrong.
I feel the Commission should present its side.
This is not to respond to Rahul Gandhi or the Opposition, but to ensure that no doubts remain in the minds of the people.”
Earlier this week, Leader of the Opposition in the Bihar Assembly Tejashwi Yadav had said reports had revealed how the BJP intends to dismantle the Constitution and democracy.
He had even asked why there was silence over the questions raised by the two Election Commissioners.
Mr. Yadav had further urged Mr. Kumar to come forward and respond to the allegations.
Mr. Kushwaha echoed the comments in a post on X. “A lot of confusion has arisen among the people over the controversy related to the SIR.
The matter needs to be addressed.
To dispel the confusion, the Election Commission should immediately come out with the clarification.”

stories.headline: NDA allies ask Election Commission to clear air on internal differences over SIR
stories.title: NDA allies ask Election Commission to clear air on internal differences over SIR
stories.summary: Opposition begins protest after the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, demanded the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Two NDA allies, Lok Janshakti Party leader and Union Minister of Food Processing Industries Chirag Paswan and Rashtriya Lok Morcha leader Upendra Kushwaha, on Friday joined the debate on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s conduct, asking the Election Commission of India to “dispel misgivings in the minds of the people” arising out of reports of alleged internal differences within the poll panel over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Though the BJP came out to defend the Election Commission of India and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, who is at the centre of controversy, Paswan stressed in Patna that “as part of the government,” he did not intend to “defend a Constitutional body”.
“Let me make it clear that, as part of the government, I do not intend to defend a constitutional body.
I am also not very worried about the allegations made by the opposition, which will always take a stand that suits it politically,” the Union Minister told reporters.

As per the news reports, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi wrote 14 times in ten days about the deletion and addition of voters to the electoral roll, as well as on other issues.
“If the people start losing trust in the electoral system, that will not augur well for democracy.
Therefore, I think the Election Commission must come out with its clarification more forcefully.
It need not respond to what Rahul Gandhi and his associates are saying, but it must dispel the misgivings in the minds of the people,” said the Hajipur MP.
Upendra Kushwaha, who is also a Rajya Sabha MP, said on X: “There is a lot of confusion among the public about SIR.
This issue needs to be addressed.
Election Commission has to clarify this without delay.”

Meanwhile, the opposition continued with its protest after the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, demanded the resignation of CEC Kumar and charged that recent elections have been rigged by the Commission.

stories.headline: Supreme Court reserves verdict on Sambhal Mosque Committee's plea against survey
stories.title: Supreme Court reserves verdict on Sambhal Mosque Committee's plea against survey
stories.summary: Supreme Court reserves verdict on Sambhal Mosque Committee's plea against survey
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday reserved its judgment on the plea filed by the Sambhal Jama Masjid Committee challenging the Allahabad High Court's order which upheld the trial court's order to appoint an advocate commissioner to survey the mosque in a suit filed by Hindu plaintiffs.

A bench comprising Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe heard arguments from Senior Advocate Huzefa Ahmadi and Advocate Nizam Pasha for the mosque committee, Advocate Hari Shankar Jain for the Hindu plaintiffs and Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj for the State of Uttar Pradesh.

The dispute arises from a civil suit filed by Hindu plaintiffs in 2024 seeking the right to access the Sambhal Jama Masjid for performing religious ceremonies on the claim that it was originally a Hindu temple which was demolished in the 16th century to build a mosque.
The trial court had appointed an Advocate Commissioner to conduct a local investigation of the mosque premises on November 19, 2024.
The Allahabad High Court, in its May 19, 2025 order, upheld the survey order and held that the suit cannot be held to be barred by the Places of Worship Act at this stage.
The mosque committee had raised its main arguments on the previous dates, and today, the plaintiffs and the State responded, with the mosque committee making rejoinder arguments at the end.
ASG KM Nataraj, appearing for the State of Uttar Pradesh, told the Court that the State did not wish to enter into the merits of the dispute since the main suit was pending trial.

"I don't want to get into the merits because the main matter is not pending before the court," Nataraj submitted, adding that the State was bound to protect the interests of both sides since the dispute concerned religious rights.
His submissions, however, focused on the interpretation of the Places of Worship Act.

Referring to Sections 2 and 3 of the Act, Nataraj submitted that Section 2 defines "conversion" to include alteration or changes, while Section 3 imposes a prohibition on conversion of a place of worship.

He pointed out that the expression "place of worship" is defined broadly and argued that the question whether a particular proceeding is barred would depend upon whether it concerns conversion of the religious character of the place.

Nataraj also referred to the provisions concerning religious denominations and Article 26 of the Constitution, submitting that the expression "religious denomination" may have to be considered in the context of the entire religion or a section thereof.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Calls For GD Entries, CCTV Footage In Plea Alleging Assam Police Custodial Torture
stories.title: Supreme Court Calls For GD Entries, CCTV Footage In Plea Alleging Assam Police Custodial Torture
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(September 25) passed an order directing the Assam Government to place on record the GD diaries, CCTV footage from the police station, and the entire record from the Gauhati High Court in a plea filed challenging the Gauhati High Court's order refusing an investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation into the alleged custodial torture of one Dipankar Gogoi.
Notice was recently issued to the Assam Government and five accused police officers in this case, and the petitioner, the sister of the deceased, was allowed to implead the CBI as a party.
It had also stayed the proceedings before the Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate for the time being.
A bench comprising Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva today briefly heard Advocate Shahrukh Alam for the petitioner.
The Court was informed that the CBI is yet to file a counter.
Shahrukh submitted that three inquiries against the police officers have taken place, including by the High Court and by the amicus, but the petitioner doesn't have any access to the records.
She added that the Police Accountability Commission also did some inquiry, the report of which is also not shared.
On this, the Court ordered all three reports to be shared with the counsel.
However, the respondent counsel objected to sharing the amicus's report.
The Court dismissed the objections and ordered that the entire record should be shared.
"Secure the entire record on the file of the Gauhati High Court.
Learned counsel for the State shall also place on record all relevant materials, GD Diaries, along with the CCTV footage by way of pen drive.
